title: Keep the pursuit viable
opening: A project may have a distant payoff and still lack the time, tools or support for its next stage. Check the conditions that let you continue, and change the route when one of them needs attention.

labels.journey: Check what keeps the pursuit viable
labels.journeyIntro: The three health bars are a metaphor. Describe actual conditions; they are not numeric diagnoses.
labels.practiceIntro: Name one next stage, what it needs, and how you will respond if conditions change.
fields: Time: what must happen before available time or a real deadline?
External resources: what is needed, and where will it come from?
Internal will: what supports interest, and what signals strain or depletion?
What change will you make, and when will you recheck?

labels.sourceQuote: The health bars are a metaphor: they do not establish that lost motivation is literally irreversible, or that curiosity removes your need for rest and support.

fields.label: Step 1: Time: identify what must happen before available time or real deadlines run out.
Step 2: External resources: identify required money, tools and support and where they will come from.
Step 3: Internal will: examine interest, strain and depletion and whether the question still draws you.
Step 4: Change the work, support, recovery or commitment where needed, then recheck as conditions change.
